title: Probing Steganographic Chain-of-Thought: Can a Cheap Classifier Spot NEST?

original_idea.body: Generate paired plain vs instructed-steganographic CoT, train simple detectors (perplexity gap, n-gram stats, logistic classifier on embeddings), and measure detection AUROC.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Cheap detectors for steganographic CoT directly support trust in CoT monitoring.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Generate plain-vs-stego CoT, train simple detectors; highly accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused detection-AUROC comparison across cheap signals; few dependencies.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Cheap no-internal-access detector, public models, lab-independent monitoring infrastructure.

novelty.reasoning: Steganographic CoT and collusion studied; cheap-detector benchmarking may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Stego CoT studied; cheap-detector comparison may be open.
